newsitem.title: UK: Pearson rises again on five-year plan.
newsitem.headline: Pearson rises again on five-year plan.

text.p: Shares in British media and leisure company Pearson Plc rose again on Tuesday following positive reaction to interim figures and targets set by new management.

Pearson shares were 23.5p higher at 716p by 0945 GMT in moderate volume of just over two million shares. Pearson stock has now added 50p from the 666p level at which it stood before Monday's interim announcement.
Pearson said profit from continuing operations almost doubled to 65.5 million stg in the first half, although the comparison was flattered by the absence this year of a number of one-off costs.
Pearson chief executive Marjorie Scardino set twin goals of annual double digit earnings growth and a doubling of the company over the next five years.
"The company is now starting to spell out its targets and gain some financial credibility," said one analyst.
"There are signs they are starting to apply some financial discipline to what had been run as an asset accumulation business," he added.

Pearson has a stellar but diverse portfolio of assets including the Financial Times newspaper, Penguin books, Madame Tussaud's waxwork museum and a television production arm. But it has long been accused of failing to get the most out of its constituent parts.

Analysts said the underlying first-half performance was encouraging. Pearson's business is weighted towards the second half of the year and full-year pre-tax profit forecasts are grouped around the 300 million stg level.
